issues.legal_issue: For a suit to recover property endowed to a religious institution, wrongful cancellation of the endowment and wrongful alienation by the settlor do not amount to the settlor’s resignation as trustee; absent additional facts establishing resignation or removal, limitation begins on the settlor’s death.
material_facts: The owner executed a valid and complete settlement endowing the properties to a temple and appointed herself as the first trustee, thereby divesting herself of ownership.
The settlor later executed a cancellation deed and alienated the endowed properties, but those acts were found to be wrongful and ineffective.
The settlor’s absence from the village, performance of worship by others, and contributions to temple expenses by devotees did not establish that she had resigned as trustee.
The plaintiffs claiming to be trustees sued to recover the properties within the limitation period measured from the settlor’s death.
issues.conclusion: The settlor did not cease to be trustee merely by executing the ineffective cancellation deed and alienating the endowed properties. No deemed resignation was established, limitation commenced on her death, and the suit was within time.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 134-B of the Limitation Act, 1908, as applied to the agreed applicable limitation provision, limitation commenced on the settlor’s death because she remained trustee until then. A trustee does not cease to be trustee by wrongfully alienating some or all trust property; similarly, an ineffective cancellation by a settlor who is trustee does not revoke the settlement or itself establish resignation. Srinivas v. Ramaswami, [1966] 3 SCR 120, recognizes that deemed resignation or removal may be inferred, but additional facts must support that inference; the conduct relied on here was insufficient.

rule.if: recovery_suit_by_endowment_trustees and valid_completed_endowment and settlor_was_trustee and wrongful_cancellation_or_alienation and not additional_facts_proving_resignation and suit_filed_within_limitation_period_from_settlors_death

predicates.recovery_suit_by_endowment_trustees: The proceeding is a suit by persons claiming to be trustees to recover property endowed to a religious institution.
predicates.valid_completed_endowment: The owner completed a valid endowment of the property and divested herself of its ownership.
predicates.settlor_was_trustee: The owner who made the endowment was appointed as a trustee of the endowed property.
predicates.wrongful_cancellation_or_alienation: The settlor later purported to cancel the endowment or alienated the endowed property, and those acts were wrongful and ineffective.
predicates.additional_facts_proving_resignation: Additional facts beyond the ineffective cancellation or wrongful alienation establish that the settlor resigned or was removed as trustee.
predicates.suit_filed_within_limitation_period_from: The recovery suit was filed within the applicable limitation period measured from the settlor’s death.

issues.definition: When trustees sue to recover property under a valid endowment, the settlor remained trustee, later cancellation or alienation was wrongful, no additional facts establish resignation, and the suit was filed within the applicable period after the settlor’s death, the suit is within limitation.

issues.legal_issue: A request to remand a case to permit evidence on an asserted deemed resignation may be refused when that ground was not specifically pleaded and the request is made late in the proceedings.
material_facts: The appellants sought a remand to present evidence on whether the settlor had deemedly resigned as trustee.
The appellants had not specifically pleaded deemed resignation in their written statement.
The request was made at a late stage, and the Court considered the passage of time and the absence of a specific plea.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused the request to remand the case for further evidence.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to permit a late evidentiary remand where the proposed ground had not been specifically pleaded, particularly at the distance of time involved. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

predicates.appeal_in_which_remand_is_sought: The proceeding is an appeal in which a party asks for the case to be remanded so it can present further evidence.
predicates.no_specific_plea_on_proposed_ground: The party did not specifically plead the ground on which it now seeks to introduce evidence.
predicates.late_request_for_additional_evidence: The party makes its request to present additional evidence at a late stage of the proceedings.

issues.definition: In an appeal, when a party seeks a late opportunity to present evidence on a ground it did not specifically plead, the remand request is denied.
